reviews.title: Many times, old school is best
reviews.body: These traps have changed very little since my dad used them when I was a child.  Hubby saw a mouse in the garage a few days back, ordered these traps, and that mouse is gone.  Bait them properly, keep them away from pets, there is nothing that works better. Glue traps are inhumane, the electric signal things are not effective.  Get these.

reviews.author: L.H.

reviews.title: Bait it correctly and it's 100% kill rate
reviews.body: These work great. I don't like the glue traps because they leave the mice alive and struggling to get away. These traps are instant kill and makes it easy to dispose of. I've baited them with everything from peanut butter to raw bacon to Laffy Taffy.Never had a miss so far, 100% kill rate. If it gets sprung it kills the mouse. The trick is how you bait it.You only need the smallest amount of bait, not some giant block of cheese. The trap has a bait holder function so take your bait and squish/squeeze it up inside the bait holder and pinch the rest off. That's all it takes. You don't need a big chunk of steak hanging off the sides. It's just a mouse, it doesn't need much food. By only leaving bait inside the bait holder section of the trap and not having big pieces hanging off it forces the mouse to interact directly with the trap and that guarantees a kill shot. If the mouse can sit off to the side of the trap and nibble on a huge chunk of bait then all you're doing is feeding them. The less bait the better. Trust.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 4, 2026

reviews.title: There simply isn't a better mousetrap
reviews.body: I have been using this style of trap for 60 years. It is simple and deadly. The mouse is dispatched humanely and completely by the snap bar rather than starving to death on a sticky trap or inside of a live catch box. Why would you want to catch and release a house mouse anyway?  The trap is inexpensive enough that I throw it out with the mouse still attached rather than trying to reuse it.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on July 20, 2026
reviews.author: Mr. Practical

reviews.title: These older style metal trigger mouse traps are absolutely the most effective types.
reviews.body: These are the best mouse traps.  The kind with the plastic paddle don't work very well.  Mice can lick the peanut butter off and not trigger the trap.  My electric traps apparently shock the mice but don't kill them.  I have mouse tracks all over the metal contact pads, but no dead mouse.  These with the small metal trigger plate work extremely well.  You don't find missing peanut butter and no mouse.  I bought these and caught three mice in three days.  They just work, no fancy claimed results, just trapped mice every time.  I am finally mouse free.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on February 27, 2026
reviews.author: Jack

reviews.title: Gold standard
reviews.body: These are 2nd best only to having too many hungry cats.The object is to smear a scent film of [peanut butter] bait on the pedal.  This causes the vermin to think the pedal is the meal therefore triggering it.  So, don't put a meals worth on trap causing your disappointment of missing bait and trap that wasn't triggered.I use wood skewers to apply bait.Set more than you think is needed since there probably are more mice than expected!
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on June 18, 2026
reviews.author: David P

reviews.title: Not for rats
reviews.body: It worked. . .  kinda.  It didn't go off the first time, so I added more bait.  It did catch the rodent the second time; unfortunately, I found out I was dealing with a rat instead of a mouse after the trap activated, and these traps aren't strong enough to kill rats, leaving it to go running through my dining room with the trap stuck on its head.  The loss of a star is due to the trap not triggering the first time the rat ate the bait.  Getting a mouse trap instead of a rat trap was my fault.  If you're unsure which type of rodent is hiding in your house, I'd suggest their larger rat traps instead.
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on April 5, 2026
reviews.author: EagleAllen
